title: Initial data loads (customers, vendors, costCodes) swallow errors silently
detail: Lines 239-241: three parallel fetches (fetchCustomers, fetchVendors, fetchCostCodes) each have `.catch(() => {})` — empty catch blocks. If any of these fail (e.g. network issue, 403), the user gets an empty customer picker / vendor drawer / cost code dropdown with zero feedback. Unlike MsaComposer (where Phase 2b added toasts for similar catches), ContractComposer was not touched because it was a newer file.
evidence: fetchCustomers().then(r => setCustomers(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {}); fetchVendors().then(r => setAllVendors(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {}); fetchCostCodes().then(r => setCostCodes(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {});
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', 'Failed to load customers/vendors/cost codes') in each catch block. Follow the pattern established by MsaComposer post-CR-0401 fix.

title: Customer-change cascading loads swallow errors silently
detail: Lines 344-354: when customerId changes, five fetches fire (fetchLocationsByCustomer, fetchContractsByCustomer, fetchCustomerApMappings, fetchKnownVendorsByCustomer). Each has a .catch that silently sets empty state. If any one fails, the user sees empty dropdowns/drawers with no error indication — they may think the customer has no locations.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', ...) to each catch. The existing pattern of resetting to empty state is correct (graceful degradation), but the user needs a visible signal that data is missing due to an error vs. genuinely absent.

title: resumeDraft has two empty catch blocks — errors are invisible
detail: Lines 578 and 590: two separate try/catch blocks inside resumeDraft have completely empty catch bodies (`catch {}`). If the detail GET or line-items fetch fails, the user sees a partially hydrated draft with no indication that data is missing. They might proceed to generate a document with stale/incomplete line items.
evidence: Line 578: `} catch {}` after apiGet for signer fields. Line 590: `} catch {}` after fetchContractLines.
recommendedFix: At minimum, toast.show('warn', 'Some draft data could not be loaded') in each catch. The user should know their resume was partial.

title: Signer inputs in inline panel have no associated labels or aria-labels
detail: Lines 816-822: four <input> elements for customer/vendor signer name and title use placeholder text only ('Full name', 'Title') with no <label>, htmlFor, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Screen readers will announce these as unlabelled text inputs. The date picker input (line 806) also lacks a label element. For external user testing, sighted users can read the placeholder, but accessible users cannot.
recommendedFix: Add aria-label attributes: aria-label="Customer signer full name", aria-label="Customer signer title", aria-label="Vendor signer full name", aria-label="Vendor signer title". Same for the date input: aria-label="Contract date".

title: Customer search input in empty state has no associated label
detail: Line 948: the customer search <input> has a placeholder but no <label>, htmlFor, or aria-label. The surrounding <h2> asks 'Who is this Work Order for?' but is not programmatically associated with the input. Same issue affects the drawer search input at line 1166.
evidence: <input autoFocus type="text" placeholder="Type to search customers..." ... />
recommendedFix: Add aria-label="Search customers" to the empty-state input. Add aria-label to the drawer search input as well ("Search vendors" or "Search locations" based on drawer type).

title: Drawer overlay backdrop lacks aria attributes and focus trap
detail: Line 1153: the drawer overlay div is a click-to-dismiss backdrop with no role, aria-label, or keyboard handling beyond the global Escape listener. Focus can tab behind the drawer into the main page. For keyboard-only users, focus management is incomplete — though the keyboard nav effect (line 265) handles arrow keys and Escape within the drawer, it does not trap focus.
evidence: <div onClick={() => setDrawer(null)} style={{ position: 'fixed', inset: 0, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.25)', zIndex: 45 }} />
recommendedFix: Add role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" to the drawer container. Add aria-label="Close drawer" and role="button" to the backdrop. Consider a simple focus trap (tabindex=-1 on the container + autoFocus on the search input, which is already present).

title: No progress indicator during 30-second document generation polling
detail: Line 857-864: The floating 'Make the Work Order' button uses disabled state during generation. However, the button text says 'Making...' but there is no spinner or progress indicator — for a 30-second polling operation, the user has no visual confirmation that work is happening.
evidence: Line 717-733: polling loop waits up to 30 seconds (6 iterations x 5s) with no progress update visible to the user except the button text 'Making...'.
recommendedFix: Add a status message or spinner below the Make button during generation, similar to MsaComposer's downloadStatus pattern.

title: DocGen polling uses $filter instead of direct GET by ID
detail: Line 723: `apiGet('/${EntitySets.documentRequests}?$filter=dcfg_document_requestid eq ${reqId}&$select=dcfg_status,dcfg_output_file_url')` — uses a $filter query to locate a record whose ID is already known. Should use a direct GET by key. The filter-based approach is less efficient and could return stale results if the portal caches list queries differently.
recommendedFix: Change to direct GET: apiGet(`/${EntitySets.documentRequests}(${reqId})?$select=dcfg_status,dcfg_output_file_url,dcfg_error_message`). Compare with MsaComposer line 343 which uses the correct direct-GET pattern.

title: WIP drafts load has empty catch — user won't know if draft resume failed
detail: Line 260: `fetchMyWIPDrafts(userEmail).then(...).catch(() => {})` — if the drafts query fails, the user won't see the resume landing even if they have drafts. Silent failure.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('warn', 'Could not load saved drafts') in the catch.

title: Hardcoded SharePoint site URL in uploadToSharePoint — breaks on non-Prod environments
detail: Line 348: `return 'https://decadesconstructiongroup.sharepoint.com/sites/DCFGContractingSuite' + raw;` — the SharePoint site URL is hardcoded. If MsaComposer runs on Test or Stage (different org URLs), the constructed SharePoint link would still point to the Prod SharePoint site.
recommendedFix: Read the SharePoint base URL from getEnvVar('dcfg_sp_site_url') or similar config key. Alternatively, require the flow to always return a full URL (not a relative path) in dcfg_output_file_url.

title: Pricing configs apiGet uses raw entity set name instead of EntitySets constant, and missing $select
detail: Line 128: `apiGet('/dcfg_pricing_configs?$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true&$orderby=createdon desc')` — two issues: (1) uses hardcoded '/dcfg_pricing_configs' instead of EntitySets.pricingConfigs (no such constant exists in portalApi.js); (2) no $select clause, returning all columns.
recommendedFix: Add `pricingConfigs: 'dcfg_pricing_configs'` to EntitySets in portalApi.js. Add $select with only the columns actually consumed.

title: MsaComposer does not import useMemo or useCallback — derived values recompute on every render
detail: Line 16: `import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';` — no useMemo or useCallback. The derived values (rate, obRate, billable, noc, moTotal, obTotal, annualMembership, totalContractValue, etc.) at lines 84-104 are recalculated on every render cycle.
evidence: Lines 84-104: const rate = loc => { ... }; const obRate = loc => { ... }; const moTotal = locs.reduce(...);
recommendedFix: Import useMemo and wrap the expensive derived values. Low priority — unlikely to cause visible lag until location count > ~200.

title: Signer form inputs have labels but no htmlFor/id association
detail: Lines 582-590: SignerForm renders <label>Signer name</label> followed by <input>. The label has no htmlFor and the input has no id. Clicking the label does not focus the input.
recommendedFix: Add id="msa-signer-name" to the input and htmlFor="msa-signer-name" to the label. Same for title.

title: MSA date and MSA name inputs have labels without htmlFor/id association
detail: Lines 567-572: the 'MSA date' and 'MSA name (optional override)' labels have no htmlFor, and their corresponding inputs have no id.
recommendedFix: Add id/htmlFor pairs: msa-date, msa-name-override, msa-new-customer-name.

title: SharePoint upload polling has no user-visible progress beyond static status text
detail: Lines 340-356: the upload polling loop runs for up to 90 seconds (18 iterations x 5s), during which the only visible indicator is the static text 'Uploading to SharePoint...'. The user may think the app has frozen.
evidence: setDownloadStatus('Uploading to SharePoint...'); const maxAttempts = 18; for (let i = 0; i < maxAttempts; i++) { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5000)); ... }
recommendedFix: Update the downloadStatus text during each poll iteration: e.g., setDownloadStatus('Uploading to SharePoint... (' + (i+1) + '/' + maxAttempts + ')').

title: Service fee input has no label association
detail: Line 615: the 'Service fee %' input has a <label> element but no htmlFor/id pairing.
evidence: <label style={labelStyle}>Service fee %</label><input type="number" step="0.01" style={inputStyle} value={serviceFee} ... />
recommendedFix: Add id="msa-service-fee" and htmlFor="msa-service-fee".

title: fetchProjects catch block swallows error with no user feedback
detail: Line 116: `.catch(function() { setLoadingProjects(false); })` — if the projects API call fails, the user sees 'No projects found.' empty state. No toast is shown.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', 'Failed to load projects') in the catch block.

title: Submit button not reset on partial failure — Promise.all project linking can leave button permanently disabled
detail: Lines 143-187: if createRfpPackage succeeds but the project-linking Promise.all fails, setSubmitting(false) is never called in that path — only in the outer .catch. The button stays disabled permanently until navigation.
evidence: Promise.all(promises).then(function() { toast.show('ok', ...); navigate(...); }); — no .catch on Promise.all, and outer .catch only fires if createRfpPackage itself fails
recommendedFix: Add .finally(() => setSubmitting(false)) on the outer promise chain. Also handle Promise.all failure with a partial-success toast.

title: RFP project links use inline @odata.bind strings instead of portalApi helpers
detail: Lines 173-176: constructs OData bind strings manually with hardcoded entity set names instead of using odataBind() helper and EntitySets constants.
recommendedFix: Import odataBind and EntitySets. Replace with odataBind('dcfg_rfp_package_id', EntitySets.rfpPackages, rfpId).

title: handleSubmit payload does not set dcfg_created_by_email
detail: Lines 147-154: the create payload has no dcfg_created_by_email. Both ContractComposer and MsaComposer set this field.
evidence: var payload = { dcfg_name: name.trim(), dcfg_trades: trades.trim(), ... dcfg_active_flag: true };
recommendedFix: Import usePortalUser, destructure userEmail, add dcfg_created_by_email: userEmail to the payload.

title: No audit log written on RFP package creation
detail: handleSubmit creates the RFP package and links projects but never calls writeAuditLog. Both ContractComposer and MsaComposer write audit logs after creation.
recommendedFix: Import writeAuditLog and AuditActionType. After creation, call writeAuditLog with targetTable: 'dcfg_rfp_package'.

title: Uses var declarations and React.createElement instead of JSX — stylistic inconsistency
detail: The entire file uses ES5-style var declarations and React.createElement calls. Every other wizard/composer uses modern const/let and JSX. Maintenance burden.
recommendedFix: Catalog only for this review. Future pass: convert to JSX + const/let.

title: Project selection checkboxes are div-based — not accessible as form controls
detail: Lines 261-287: each project option is a <div> with onClick and a visual checkbox (styled div). No role='checkbox', no aria-checked, no keyboard handling. Screen readers cannot announce these as checkboxes.
recommendedFix: Add role='checkbox', aria-checked={isSelected}, tabIndex=0, and onKeyDown handler (Space/Enter) to each project div.
